name: cliffs_of_moher
title: Cliffs of Moher, County Clare, Ireland
note: Shale and sandstone sea cliffs rising 120-214 m straight out of the Atlantic for 8 km, from Hag's Head north past O'Brien's Tower.
grid: local azimuthal equidistant (sphere R=6371008.8 m) centred on centre_lat/centre_lon; x east, y north; row 0 = north edge; pixel centre x = (col + 0.5 - cols/2) * pixel_size_m, y = (rows/2 - row - 0.5) * pixel_size_m
data_note: Copernicus GLO-30 (30 m) cannot resolve a vertical 200 m face: here the cliff is a steep ramp one or two source pixels wide. The plan of the coast and the cliff-top plateau are right; seven_sisters is the high-resolution (2 m lidar) reference for the vertical cliff itself.
sea_floor: every height at or below 0.3 m is set to -2 m: the sea surface is 0 m and the source's bathymetry is left out; 0 offshore patches of the source's sea data (each under 5% of the mainland) are sea as well

source.dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (public), 1 arc-second, AWS Open Data copernicus-dem-30m
source.licence: Copernicus DEM licence for GLO-30 Public: free, worldwide, any lawful use, attribution required; https://spacedata.copernicus.eu/documents/20123/122407/GEO1988-CopernicusDEM-SPE-002_ProductHandbook_I5.0+%281%29.pdf
source.attribution: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved
source.caveat: A digital SURFACE model: it includes forest canopy and buildings.
source.resampling: bicubic (upsampled 4.9x from the source grid: no detail finer than the native resolution), then Gaussian sigma 0.60 source px (17.6 m) against the radar speckle and the source lattice

encoding: 16-bit greyscale PNG: height_m = height_min_m + v / 65535 * (height_max_m - height_min_m)
water_mask_encoding: 8-bit: 0 land, 255 sea, 128 + i the i-th lake of `water`
